nahhas-irab:1-1.t: The reading of the people of Medina and of Abū ʿAmr is without imāla (inclining the vowel toward i), and the reading of the Kufans is with imāla, except ʿĀṣim, from whom there is a disagreement in transmission. Abū Jaʿfar said: According to most of the scholars of Arabic there is no justification for imāla here, for two reasons. One is that there is neither a yāʾ nor a kasra here to bring about imāla. The other reason is that the ṭāʾ is one of the letters that prevent imāla. These are two clear reasons. Some grammarians, however, chose imāla. Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn al-Sarī said: One who gives «طه» a kasra inclines it toward kasra, because in the shortened noun (al-maqṣūr) the kasra predominates by way of imāla. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is not a proof; imāla is not permissible in many shortened nouns. But Sībawayh claimed that imāla is permissible in the letters of the alphabet, so one says «با تا ثا», because they are nouns; so a distinction is made between them and particles such as «لا», which is not given imāla because it is a particle. Abū Isḥāq said: For one who reads طه ما أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ لِتَشْقى, the original form according to him is «طأ», i.e. "tread the ground with both your feet in prayer"; the hamza was replaced by hāʾ, just as one says «إيّاك» and «هيّاك», and «أرقت الماء» and «هرقت الماء». He said: It may also be on the basis of replacing the hamza, so that the original is «ط» ("tread") — "O you!" — then the hāʾ was brought to clarify the vowel in the pause.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: Some grammarians say this is the lām of negation (lām al-nafy), and some say it is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd). Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān say of the like of it: it is the lām of the genitive (lām al-khafḍ), and the meaning according to him is: "We did not send down the Qurʾān to you for distress." «الشقاء» is pronounced long and short, and it has a wāw as its root letter.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: Abū Isḥāq said: It is a badal (substitute) from «يشقى», i.e. "We sent it down only as a reminder." Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a far-fetched interpretation; the closer one is that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) or as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: تَنْزِيلًا A maṣdar (verbal noun). مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ وَالسَّماواتِ الْعُلى According to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, the like of this cannot come except with alif and lām, and that is the view of the Kufans. He said: It is impossible to say «سقطت له ثنيّتان علييان لا سفليان» ("two upper front teeth fell out, not two lower ones"), because only the definite is intended by it; if you intend the indefinite and the preference of one thing over another, you bring «من» and say «سقطت له ثنية أعلى من كذا» ("a front tooth higher than such-and-such fell out").

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: The accusative is also permissible, as praise. Abū Isḥāq said: The genitive is also permissible, as a badal (substitute) from «من». Saʿīd ibn Masʿada said: The nominative means "He is the Most Merciful." Abū Jaʿfar said: The nominative is also permissible as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and as a badal from the latent pronoun in «خلق».

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ In the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). وَما بَيْنَهُما وَما تَحْتَ الثَّرى is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: وَإِنْ تَجْهَرْ بِالْقَوْلِ Jussive (majzūm) by the condition, and the apodosis is فَإِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ السِّرَّ وَأَخْفى, i.e. "and what is more hidden than it."

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ Nominative as a badal (substitute) from what is in «يعلم» [i.e. its latent pronoun], or with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or as a mubtadaʾ. لَهُ الْأَسْماءُ الْحُسْنى Nominative as a mubtadaʾ; الْحُسْنى is its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: Ḥamza read فَقالَ لِأَهْلِهِ امْكُثُوا [Translator's note: i.e. «لِأَهْلِهُ» with ḍamma on the hāʾ, as the following explanation shows], and likewise in al-Qaṣaṣ. Abū Jaʿfar said: This follows the dialect of those who say «مررت بهو يا هذا»; he brought it in its original form, and it is permissible, except that Ḥamza departed from his own principle in these two places specifically.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: Because the meaning of «نودي» is "it was said to him." Al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAmr read «نودي يا موسى أنّي» with fatḥa on the hamza, meaning "he was called with (بأنّي) …," and «أنّ» is in the position of an accusative. For one who reads with kasra, the meaning according to him is: "He said: Indeed I…."

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: The people of Medina and the people of Basra read «بالواد المقدّس طوى» without tanwīn, and the people of Kufa read طُوىً with tanwīn. Abū Jaʿfar said: The proper way is to omit the tanwīn, because it is like «عمر», shifted from its pattern (maʿdūl) and definite. It may also be the name of the spot (al-buqʿa), so it is likewise a diptote. As for one who gives tanwīn, Abū Isḥāq claimed that he takes it to be the name of the place, not shifted, like «حطم» and «صرد». He said: One who says «طوى» (ṭiwan) and declines it fully makes it like «ضلع» and «معى», as the name of the place; and it may also be a diptote as the name of the spot. Abū Jaʿfar said: One who takes «طوى» in the sense of «ثنى» (twice) gives it tanwīn and nothing else, taking it from «ثنيت الشيء ثنى», i.e. it was sanctified twice. In the ḥadīth: "There is no thinā in charity," i.e. it is not doubled so as to be taken twice.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: The people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read وَأَنَا اخْتَرْتُكَ, and the rest of the Kufans read «وإنّا اخترناك». The meaning is the same, except that «وأنا اخترتك» is preferable here for two reasons. One is that it more closely resembles the written form; the second is that it fits better the sequence of the speech, because of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: يا مُوسى إِنِّي أَنَا رَبُّكَ, and the address proceeded in this sequence.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي Abū Isḥāq said: There are two views on it. The meaning may be: "Establish prayer so that you remember Me in it," because prayer exists only with remembrance. The other view: "Establish prayer whenever you remember it," that being the time of the prayer. Abū Jaʿfar said: There is a third view: the meaning may be "Establish prayer so that I may mention you with praise." Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Abū Rajāʾ and al-Shaʿbī read أَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي [Translator's note: the vowelling shown is that of the standard text; the following discussion shows the variant ends in alif, i.e. «لِذِكْرَى»]. This reading has two interpretations. One is that this alif is the alif of the feminine. The other is that this alif replaces the yāʾ, as one says «يا غلاما أقبل»; this was done so that the verse-endings agree.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ أَكادُ أُخْفِيها A difficult verse. Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned something of what has been said about it. From Saʿīd ibn Jubayr there are two transmissions. One is what al-Ḥasan ibn al-Faraj narrated to us in Gaza; he said: Yūsuf ibn ʿAdī narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn Sahl al-Kūfī narrated to us, from Warqāʾ — he is Ibn Iyās — from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, that he read أَكادُ أُخْفِيها with fatḥa on the hamza [i.e. «أَخْفِيها»]; he said: "I reveal it." This transmission has no route other than this; Abū ʿUbayd transmitted it from al-Kisāʾī, from this Muḥammad ibn Sahl. Better than this chain is what Yaḥyā al-Qaṭṭān transmitted from al-Thawrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, that he read أَكادُ أُخْفِيها with ḍamma on the hamza. Abū Jaʿfar said: One says «خفى الشيء يخفيه» when he reveals it; and it has been reported that one says «أخفاه» when he reveals it, but that is not well known. Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān, when the meaning of «أخفيها» was difficult for him, turn to this view, and he said its meaning is like the meaning of «أَخفيها», i.e. "I reveal it." Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning is not "I reveal it," especially since «أَخفيها» is an anomalous (shādhdh) reading; how could we refer the sound, widespread reading to the anomalous one? The meaning of the ḍamma reading is preferable, and the implied form is: "The Hour is coming — I almost bring it"; «آتية» indicates «آتي بها»; then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: أُخْفِيها as a new beginning. This is a sound meaning, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has hidden the Hour, which is the Day of Resurrection, and the hour in which a person dies, so that a person keeps working while the matter remains obscure to him and does not delay repentance. It was also said: the meaning is "I almost hide it," i.e. I come close to that, because when you say «كاد زيد يقوم» ("Zayd almost stood"), it may be that he stood and it may be that he did not; and it was shown that He has hidden it by evidence other than this, on this answer. It was also said: the meaning is "The Hour is coming لِتُجْزى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِما تَسْعى," and it was said:
the meaning is "Establish prayer for My remembrance, so that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives."

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: فَلا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْها i.e. from belief in it and in what it contains, مَنْ لا يُؤْمِنُ بِها وَاتَّبَعَ هَواهُ i.e. in disbelief in it. فَتَرْدى from «ردي يردى», when one perishes.

nahhas-irab:17-18.t:
وَما تِلْكَ A mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and it carries the sense of drawing attention. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that «تلك» here is an incomplete noun (ism nāqiṣ) whose ṣila (relative clause) is «بيمينك». Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw Abū Isḥāq inclining to this view and holding it; the meaning according to both of them is "And what is that which is in your right hand?" I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I heard Abū al-ʿAbbās reject this view, saying: It is not permissible for the vague nouns [demonstratives] to take a ṣila. One says:
أَهُشُّ and «أهشّ» [Translator's note: the second form presumably «أَهِشُّ», with kasra; the source does not vowel it].

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: فَأَلْقاها فَإِذا هِيَ حَيَّةٌ A mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The accusative is also permissible: one says «خرجت فإذا زيد جالس» and «جالسا», as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Jaʿfar said: We have explained it earlier. The pause is «حيه», with hāʾ.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: سَنُعِيدُها سِيرَتَهَا الْأُولى Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: the implied form is «إلى سيرتها» ("to its state"), like وَاخْتارَ مُوسى قَوْمَهُ [al-Aʿrāf: 155]. He said: It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of «سنعيدها» is "We shall make it go (سنسيّرها)."

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
وَاضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلى جَناحِكَ Outside the Qurʾān «ضمّ» is permissible with fatḥa, kasra or ḍamma on the mīm because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. The fatḥa is best because of its lightness; the kasra is according to the base rule; and the ḍamma is by assimilation (itbāʿ). If you bring alif and lām [after it], the kasra is best; if you bring an absent (third-person) pronoun, the ḍamma is more frequent, as is making the doubling overt, because the second letter has become vowelless. «يد» has as its original form «يدي», on the pattern faʿl; this is shown by «أيد», and its diminutive is «يديّة» because it is feminine. تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ Accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is a diptote because it contains the two alifs of the feminine, which never leave it, so their being inseparable is like a second cause; therefore it is a diptote even when indefinite. The hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa] differs from it, because the hāʾ can be separated from the noun. آيَةً أُخْرى Al-Akhfash said: As a badal (substitute) from «بيضاء». This is a good view, because the meaning in «بيضاء» is "made manifest." Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is "We have given you another sign," or "We give you a sign," because when He said تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ it indicated that He had given him another sign. He said:
«آية» in the nominative is also permissible, meaning "this is a sign."

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: i.e. he has transgressed all bounds in disbelief.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: i.e. widen it and make easy for me the performance of what You have commanded me.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: He did not say "untie every knot from my tongue"; for that reason Pharaoh said: «ولا يكاد يبين» ("and he can scarcely express himself").

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: Jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request.

nahhas-irab:29-30.t: It may be by way of advancing and postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr), the two being objects (mafʿūlān), with «الأخ» as a naʿt (adjective); the implied form is "and make Hārūn my brother a minister for me." «هارون» may also be a badal (substitute) from «وزير», because the definite may be substituted for the indefinite. The nominative is also permissible.

nahhas-irab:31-32.t: As a supplication. It is transmitted from al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq that they read اشْدُدْ ] with fatḥa on the hamza, ḍamma on the first dāl and sukūn on the second [i.e. «أَشْدُدْ»], and وَأَشْرِكْهُ with ḍamma on the hamza and sukūn on the kāf [i.e. «وَأُشْرِكْهُ»], making the two verbs in the position of a jussive (jazm) as the answer to his saying «اجعل لي وزيرا من أهلي». [Translator's note: the bracket after «اشدد» is as in the source.] This reading is anomalous (shādhdh) and far-fetched, because the answer to the like of this is jussive only with the sense of condition and requital, so the meaning would be: "If You make for me a minister from my family, I will strengthen my back through him and I will make him share in my affair." His affair is prophethood and the mission, and this was not up to him ﷺ so that he could announce it; rather, he asks Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to make him share with him in prophethood. From Ibn ʿAbbās: «أشدد به أزري» means "strengthen me," and from him also: "my back." Abū Jaʿfar said: It is derived from «الإزار» (the waist-wrap), because it is tightened. The back is also called «أزر» because of the strength in it. «آزره» means "he strengthened him." «وزير» is not from this; it is derived only from «الوزر», which is a mountain [i.e. a refuge].

nahhas-irab:33-35.t: كَيْ نُسَبِّحَكَ كَثِيراً A naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "much glorification"; it may also be a naʿt of a time. Assimilation (idghām) is good, and likewise وَنَذْكُرَكَ كَثِيراً is assimilated, and likewise إِنَّكَ كُنْتَ بِنا بَصِيراً, because the two letters belong to two words. «بصيرا» means "knowing what is good for us."

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: أَنِ اقْذِفِيهِ فِي التَّابُوتِ فَاقْذِفِيهِ The pronoun refers to the chest. فَلْيُلْقِهِ الْيَمُّ بِالسَّاحِلِ An imperative. Al-Farrāʾ said: It carries the sense of requital (mujāzāt), i.e. "cast him, and the sea will throw him up." Likewise, according to him, is اتَّبِعُوا سَبِيلَنا وَلْنَحْمِلْ خَطاياكُمْ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 12]. وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلى عَيْنِي i.e. under My knowledge of you. Assimilation (idghām) is permissible but not as good as in the first, because of the remoteness of the guttural letters.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلى قَدَرٍ يا مُوسى At the time when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, willed to send him.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: i.e. I strengthened you and taught you, so that you may convey My commands and prohibitions to My servants.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: اذْهَبْ أَنْتَ وَأَخُوكَ Conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the latent pronoun; conjoining to it is good because you have emphasised it [with «أنت»].

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: إِنَّهُ طَغى i.e. he has transgressed all bounds in disbelief.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشى Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned it.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t:
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «يفرط» means "hasten," and he said: «يطغى» means "transgress." Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied form is:
"We fear that some matter will proceed hastily from him against us," i.e. some matter will rush out. Al-Farrāʾ said: One says «فرط منه أمر» (a matter came hastily from him). He said: «أفرط» means "went to excess," and he said: «فرّط» means "neglected." Abū Isḥāq said: Its root, in all of it, is from going ahead (al-taqdīm).

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: إِنَّنِي مَعَكُما أَسْمَعُ وَأَرى i.e. I hear his speech and see his action, and I will not leave him free to deal with you.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: وَالسَّلامُ عَلى مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الْهُدى Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. whoever follows guidance is safe from the wrath of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His punishment. He said: It is not a greeting; and the proof of that is that it is not the beginning of an encounter nor of an address. Zāʾida transmitted from al-Aʿmash that he read الَّذِي أَعْطى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلْقَهُ with fatḥa on the lām [i.e. «خَلَقَهُ», as a verb]. [Translator's note: this phrase is from verse 50.]

nahhas-irab:51-52.t:
قالَ فَما بالُ الْقُرُونِ الْأُولى He said: How will they be brought to life and requited? — i.e. this is far-fetched. So Mūsā ﷺ answered him that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows them. قالَ عِلْمُها عِنْدَ رَبِّي فِي كِتابٍ There are two views on its meaning:
One is that it is a figurative representation (tamthīl majāz); the other is that it is literal, and that this is written and the angels read it and draw from it evidence of the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His greatness. لا يَضِلُّ رَبِّي وَلا يَنْسى There are three views on its meaning:
Abū Isḥāq mentioned one of them, that it is a naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب», i.e. "my Lord does not lose it nor forget it." The second view is that the sentence is complete, then He began anew and said: "My Lord does not go astray," i.e. does not perish, from His saying «أإذا ضللنا في الأرض» ("When we are lost in the earth…"), "and does not forget anything." The third view, the closest to the meaning: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed that He has no need of a book; so the meaning is that knowledge of nothing at all escapes Him, nor awareness of it, and He does not forget His knowledge of it. Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, ʿĪsā and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read فِي كِتابٍ لا يَضِلُّ رَبِّي [Translator's note: i.e. «لا يُضِلُّ», with ḍamma on the yāʾ, as the gloss shows], i.e. "my Lord does not let it be lost nor forget it."

nahhas-irab:53-53.t: الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ مَهْداً The Kufans read مَهْداً [Translator's note: the others read «مهادا»], and «مهادا» is preferable here, because «مهدا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and this is not a place for a maṣdar except by omission, i.e. "possessing a cradle." وَسَلَكَ لَكُمْ فِيها سُبُلًا Figurative, i.e. He made paths for you in it. وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً i.e. from its regions.

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: مِنْها خَلَقْناكُمْ i.e. from the earth. Abū Isḥāq said: Because Ādam ﷺ was created from the earth. Someone other than Abū Isḥāq said: the sperm-drop is created from dust; the apparent sense of the Qurʾān indicates this.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْناهُ آياتِنا كُلَّها The meaning is: "We showed Pharaoh all Our signs which We gave to Mūsā ﷺ." The benefit in this is that Pharaoh saw all the signs with his own eyes, not by report. فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبى to believe.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t:
فَاجْعَلْ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِداً لا نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلا أَنْتَ مَكاناً سُوىً.
The Kufans read سُوىً with ḍamma on the sīn; the kasra is better known and more familiar. It was said: its meaning is "other than that place." The people of tafsīr hold that the meaning of «سوى» is "halfway and fair," and this is a good view. Its root is from your saying «جلس في سواء الدار», i.e. in its middle, and «في سواها». The middle of everything is its fairest part. In the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ on وَكَذلِكَ جَعَلْناكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطاً [al-Baqara: 143]: i.e. just. Zuhayr said: [al-Wāfir] 290-
أرونا خطّة لا ضيم فيها ... يسوّى بيننا فيها السّواء
(Show us a course with no injustice in it, in which fairness is made equal between us.)

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: قالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ A mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is "the time of your appointment is the Day of Adornment." Al-Ḥasan read مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ as an adverb (ẓarf) [Translator's note: i.e. «يَوْمَ» in the accusative; the source shows the standard vowelling]. Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. it occurs on the Day of Adornment. وَأَنْ يُحْشَرَ النَّاسُ ضُحًى «أن» is in the position of a nominative — meaning, according to the reading of one who reads «يوم الزينة» as an adverb, while وَأَنْ يُحْشَرَ النَّاسُ has the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), so one of them cannot be conjoined to the other except by an omission, meaning "and the day on which the people are gathered." Better than this is that «أن» be in the position of a genitive, conjoined to «الزينة». «الضحى» is feminine; the Arabs form its diminutive without hāʾ, so that its diminutive will not resemble the diminutive of «ضحوة».

nahhas-irab:61-61.t:
قالَ لَهُمْ مُوسى وَيْلَكُمْ In the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun). Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. may Allah, Mighty and Majestic, attach woe to them. He said: It may also be a muḍāf (genitive construct) in the vocative. فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ بِعَذابٍ The answer to the prohibition. The Kufans read فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ [Translator's note: the source shows a single vowelling; the two readings are «فَيَسْحَتَكُمْ» and «فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ»]. The first is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz and this one the dialect of Banū Tamīm. Al-Farazdaq said: [al-Ṭawīl] 291-
وعضّ زمان يا ابن مروان لم يدع ... من المال إلّا مسحتا أو مجلّف
(And the bite of a time, O son of Marwān, that left of wealth nothing but what was destroyed or stripped bare.)
The meaning of لا تَفْتَرُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً is: "Do not say that the proofs I bring are sorcery." وَقَدْ خابَ مَنِ افْتَرى i.e. he has been disappointed of mercy and reward.

nahhas-irab:62-63.t:
قالُوا إِنْ هذانِ لَساحِرانِ There are six readings of it. The Medinans and the Kufans read «إنّ هذان لساحران»; Abū ʿAmr read «إنّ هذين لساحران», and this reading is transmitted from al-Ḥasan, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī. Al-Zuhrī, Ismāʿīl ibn Qusṭanṭīn, al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad and ʿĀṣim, in one of the two transmissions, read إِنْ هذانِ لَساحِرانِ with «إن» lightened.
These are three readings which the community transmitted from the leading authorities. It is transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: «إن هذان إلّا ساحران». Al-Kisāʾī said: In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is «إن هذان ساحران» without lām. Al-Farrāʾ said: In the codex (ḥarf) of Ubayy it is «إن ذان إلّا ساحران». These are three further readings, to be taken as explanation (tafsīr); except that it is permissible to recite with them [Translator's note: so in the source, «إلا أنها جائز أن يقرأ بها لمخالفتها المصحف», "except that it is permissible to recite with them because they contradict the muṣḥaf"; the sense required is evidently "not permissible," and a negation has probably dropped out] because they contradict the muṣḥaf. Abū Jaʿfar said: On the first reading the scholars have six views. Among them is that «إنّ» means "yes" (naʿam), as al-Kisāʾī reported from ʿĀṣim; he said: The Arabs
use «إنّ» in the sense of "yes." Sībawayh reported that «إنّ» comes in the sense of «أجل» ("yes, indeed"). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd and Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq used to hold this view. Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw Abū Isḥāq and Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān holding it. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān narrated to us; he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Salām al-Naysābūrī narrated to us — then I met this ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad and he narrated to me; he said: ʿUmayr ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Nawfalī, of the descendants of al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, narrated to us; he said: ʿAmr ibn Jumayʿ al-Kūfī narrated to us, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from ʿAlī — that is, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn — from his father, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. He said: I cannot count how many times I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say on his pulpit: "إنّ الحمد لله, we praise Him and seek His help," then he would say: "I am the most eloquent of all Quraysh, and the most eloquent of them after me is Abān ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ." ] [Translator's note: the bracket is as in the source.] Abū Muḥammad said: ʿUmayr said: Its i'rab according to the scholars of Arabic grammar is «إنّ الحمدَ لله» in the accusative, except that the Arabs put «إنّ» in the sense of "yes," as if he meant: "Yes, praise belongs to Allah." That is because the orators of the Jāhiliyya used to open their speeches with «نعم» ("yes"). The poet said, in the sense of "yes": [al-Kāmil] 292-
قالوا: غدرت فقلت إنّ وربّما ... نال العلى وشفى الغليل الغادر
(They said: "You have betrayed." I said: "Yes — and often the betrayer attains the heights and slakes his thirst for vengeance.")
And Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt said: [Majzūʾ al-Kāmil] 293-
بكر العواذل في الصّبوح ... يلمنني وألومهنّه
ويقلن شيب قد علاك ... وقد كبرت، فقلت: إنّه
(The censuring women came early at the morning draught, blaming me while I blamed them; they say: "Grey hair has come over you and you have grown old." I said: "Yes, it is so.")
On this basis it is permissible that the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, إِنْ هذانِ لَساحِرانِ be in the sense of "yes."
Abū Jaʿfar said: Dāwūd ibn al-Haytham recited to me; he said: Thaʿlab recited to me: [al-Khafīf] 294-
ليت شعري هل للمحبّ شفاء ... من جوى حبّهنّ إنّ اللّقاء
(Would that I knew: is there a cure for the lover from the burning of his love for them? Yes — the meeting.)
i.e. "yes." This is one view. Abū Zayd, al-Kisāʾī, al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said: This is according to the dialect of Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb. Al-Farrāʾ said: They say «رأيت الزّيدان» and «مررت بالزّيدان», and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 295-
فأطرق إطراق الشّجاع ولو يرى ... مساغا لناباه الشّجاع لصمّما
(He lowered his head as the serpent lowers its head; had the serpent seen an opening for its two fangs, it would have bitten deep.)
Abū al-Khaṭṭāb reported that this is the dialect of Banū Kināna. Al-Farrāʾ has another view; he said: I found the alif to be a prop (diʿāma), not the final radical of the word, so I added a nūn to it and did not change it, just as you say «الذي» and then add a nūn to it, saying «جاءني الذين عندك» and «رأيت الذين عندك». Abū Jaʿfar said: It was also said: the alif in your saying «هذان» was likened to the alif in «يفعلان», so it was not changed. Abū Isḥāq said: The early grammarians say the hāʾ here is implied, and the meaning is «إنّه هذان لساحران» ("indeed, the matter is: these two are sorcerers"). These are five views. Abū Jaʿfar said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān about this verse, and he said: If you wish, I will answer you with the answer of the grammarians, and if you wish, I will answer you with my own view. I said: With your own view. He said: Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq asked me about it, and I said: The view I hold is that since «هذا» is said in the position of the nominative, the accusative and the genitive in one and the same state, and the dual ought not to change the singular for it, the dual was treated like the singular. He said: How fine this would be if someone had preceded you in saying it, so that one could feel at ease with it. I said: Then let the judge say it, so that one may feel at ease with it. And he smiled. Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is the best, except that there is something in it, because one only says «نعم زيد خارج» ("Yes, Zayd is going out"), and the lām scarcely occurs here — although the grammarians have discussed this and said: the lām is intended to come first. Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is «إنّ هذان لهما ساحران» ("Yes, these two — they are sorcerers"), then the mubtadaʾ (subject) was omitted, as the poet said: [al-Rajaz] 296-
أمّ الحليس لعجوز شهربه
(Umm al-Ḥulays is surely a decrepit old woman.)
The second view is among the best ways the verse has been interpreted, since this dialect is well known and has been reported by those whose knowledge, truthfulness and trustworthiness are approved — among them Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī, who is the one who says: "When Sībawayh says 'someone I trust told me,' he means only me"; and Abū al-Khaṭṭāb al-Akhfash, who is one of the leading masters of the language, from whom Sībawayh and others transmitted. Among the clearest things on this is the saying of Sībawayh: "Know that when you make the singular dual you add two added letters to it, the first of them being a letter of prolongation and softness, and it is the letter of inflection (ḥarf al-iʿrāb)." Abū Jaʿfar said: Sībawayh's saying "and it is the letter of inflection" requires that in principle it does not change. «إنّ هذان» came in its original form so that this would be known; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: اسْتَحْوَذَ عَلَيْهِمُ الشَّيْطانُ [al-Mujādila: 19] and did not say «استحاذ»; it came in this way to indicate the original form, since the leading authorities transmitted it and it became clear that it is the original. This is very clear. وَيَذْهَبا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ الْمُثْلى The feminine of «أمثل», just as one says «الأفضل» and «الفضلى». «الطريقة» was made feminine according to the wording, even though men are meant by it; the feminine may also be according to the sense of the group.

nahhas-irab:64-64.t:
فَأَجْمِعُوا كَيْدَكُمْ is the reading of the people of the great cities, except Abū ʿAmr, who read «فاجمعوا» with the connecting hamza (waṣl) and fatḥa on the mīm, arguing from His saying, Mighty and Majestic: فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَتى [Ṭāhā: 60]. In what is reported from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, he said: Abū ʿAmr's own argument obliges him to read contrary to this reading of his — namely the reading which most people follow. He said: Because he argued from «جمع», and His saying, Mighty and Majestic, فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ has already established this, so it is unlikely that after it comes «فاجمعوا», and likely that after it comes «فأجمعوا», i.e. "resolve and be earnest"; since that had preceded, this one must differ from it in meaning.
One says: «أمر مجمع عليه» (a matter resolved upon). Abū Jaʿfar said: The justification of Abū ʿAmr's reading is: "gather every plot and every stratagem and join it with its fellow." ثُمَّ ائْتُوا صَفًّا Accusative because the verb falls on it. As for the saying of Abū ʿUbayda: he said one says «أتيت الصفّ», i.e. the place of prayer; so the meaning according to him is "come to the place where you gather on the day of the festival." Abū Isḥāq claimed that it may be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:66-66.t:
Hārūn the reader said: The dialect of Banū Tamīm is «عصيهم» (with kasra on the ʿayn), and al-Ḥasan follows it. Abū Jaʿfar said: One who gives the ʿayn kasra makes the kasra follow the kasra, and we have mentioned it. يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّها تَسْعى Abū Isḥāq said: «أنّ» is in the position of a nominative, i.e. "their moving was made to appear to him." Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the position of «أنّ» is accusative, i.e. «بأنها», then the bāʾ was omitted. Al-Ḥasan read «تخيّل» with tāʾ. Abū ʿUbayd said: He meant the ropes. Abū Isḥāq said: One who reads with tāʾ makes «أنّ» in the position of an accusative, i.e. "they appeared to him as moving things." He said: It may also be in the position of a nominative as a badal (substitute) — a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl) — as Sībawayh reported: «ما لي بهم علم أمرهم», i.e. "I have no knowledge of their affair." He said: And he recited: [al-Rajaz] 297-
وذكرت تقتد برد مائها
(And she remembered Taqtud, the coolness of its water.)
i.e. she remembered the coolness of the water of Taqtud.

nahhas-irab:67-68.t: فَأَوْجَسَ فِي نَفْسِهِ خِيفَةً مُوسى It is said that he feared the people would be led astray when the sorcerers threw their ropes and staffs. They were far from the people, on one side; Pharaoh and his troops on another side; and Mūsā and Hārūn, Allah bless them both, on another side. So Mūsā ﷺ feared that the matter would be made confusing to the people, since they imagined that the ropes and staffs were moving and that they were snakes, and so they would fancy that the sorcerers had equalled Mūsā ﷺ in what he brought. It is also said that Mūsā ﷺ feared only because the command to throw the staff was delayed for him; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: لا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْأَعْلى, i.e. do not fear the confusion, for We shall make your matter clear so that you prevail over them with the proof.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t:
وَأَلْقِ ما فِي يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ ما صَنَعُوا So he threw the staff, and it swallowed up their ropes and staffs, which were the load of three hundred camels; then it returned to being a staff, and no one knows where the ropes and staffs went except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Abū Isḥāq said: The original form of «خيفة» is «خوفة»; the wāw was replaced by yāʾ because of the kasra before it.
He said: تَلْقَفْ ما صَنَعُوا in the nominative is also permissible [i.e. «تلقفُ»], being an imperfect verb in the position of an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial).
He said: «أنّ ما صنعوا» with fatḥa on the hamza is also permissible, i.e. "because what…." كَيْدُ ساحِرٍ in the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ», with «ما» in the sense of «الذي»; the accusative [«كيدَ»] is on the basis that «ما» is the restraining «ما» (kāffa). The Kufans except ʿĀṣim read «كيد سحر», annexing the type to the genus, as you say «ثوب خزّ» ("a garment of silk").

nahhas-irab:71-71.t: إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ الَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ السِّحْرَ The pronoun refers back to Mūsā ﷺ. Pharaoh used this as a ruse to confuse the people, saying to the sorcerers: "Mūsā is your chief," i.e. he is more skilled in sorcery than you, and he colluded with you in this and taught it to you. So he cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides and crucified them until they died. وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنا أَشَدُّ عَذاباً وَأَبْقى Abū Isḥāq said: «أيّ» is nominative because its form is the form of interrogation, so what precedes it does not act on it, since that is a statement.

nahhas-irab:72-72.t:
Abū Isḥāq said: «الذي» is in the position of a genitive by conjunction. The meaning is: "We will not prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us, nor over Allah, Mighty and Majestic." He said: It may also be in the position of a genitive as an oath.
فَاقْضِ ما أَنْتَ قاضٍ The yāʾ is dropped in connected speech because it is vowelless and the tanwīn is vowelless; and it is dropped in the pause to indicate that in connected speech it is without yāʾ. Sībawayh chose to retain it in the pause, because the cause — the meeting of two vowelless letters — has gone. إِنَّما تَقْضِي هذِهِ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا Accusative as an adverb (ẓarf). The meaning is: "You only decide in the enjoyment of this worldly life." Al-Farrāʾ allowed the nominative, taking «ما» in the sense of «الذي».

nahhas-irab:73-73.t: «ما» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to «الخطايا». It was also said: it has no position and is negating, i.e. "that He may forgive us our sins of sorcery, and you did not compel us to it." The first is preferable.

nahhas-irab:74-74.t: إِنَّهُ مَنْ يَأْتِ رَبَّهُ مُجْرِماً The hāʾ is an allusion to the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ».

nahhas-irab:77-77.t:
«أَنْ أَسْرِ» from «أسرى», and «أنِ اسْرِ» from «سرى»: two eloquent dialects. فَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقاً فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَساً لا تَخافُ دَرَكاً is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī; al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read «لا تخف دركا». The first reading is clearer, because after it comes وَلا تَخْشى, agreed upon without jussive. The first reading has three interpretations: it may be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of «طريق», with an omission in it [i.e. "in which you do not fear"]; or cut off from what precedes [i.e. resumptive]. The second reading has two interpretations: one is the jussive of prohibition, and the other is the jussive as the answer to the imperative, namely «فاضرب». As for وَلا تَخْشى when you make «لا تخف» jussive, the grammarians have two interpretations of it. One — and it is the only one permissible — is that it is cut off from the first, like يُوَلُّوكُمُ الْأَدْبارَ ثُمَّ لا يُنْصَرُونَ [Āl ʿImrān: 111]. The other interpretation — al-Farrāʾ mentioned it ] [Translator's note: the bracket is as in the source] — is that «ولا تخشى» is intended as jussive while the yāʾ [i.e. the final letter] is retained in it; he claimed it is as the poet said: [al-Basīṭ] 298-
هجوت زبّان ثمّ جئت معتذرا ... من سبّ زبّان لم تهجو ولم تدع
(You satirised Zabbān, then came apologising for reviling Zabbān — you neither satirised nor left it alone.)
And he recited: [al-Wāfir] 299-
ألم يأتيك والأنباء تنمى ... بما لاقت لبون بني زياد
(Has it not reached you — and news spreads — what befell the milch-camels of Banū Ziyād?)
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is among the ugliest of errors — to interpret the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by anomalies of poetry. Moreover, the poetry he brought does not resemble the verse at all, because the wāw and the yāʾ differ from the alif, since they can take a vowel and the alif cannot; so the poet, when compelled, may suppose them to be voweled and then drop the vowel for the jussive, but this is impossible with the alif. Moreover, there is no metrical necessity in the two verses requiring this, because if they are transmitted with the wāw and the yāʾ dropped, they are sound metre of al-Basīṭ and al-Wāfir; al-Khalīl calls the first maṭwī and the second manqūṣ.

nahhas-irab:78-78.t: In the sense of magnifying [the event] and knowledge of the matter.

nahhas-irab:79-79.t: i.e. he led them away from right guidance, and did not guide them to any good or salvation, because he reckoned that Mūsā ﷺ and those who followed him could not escape him, since the sea was before them. When Mūsā ﷺ struck the sea with his staff, twelve paths split open in it, with the water standing between the paths like mountains, and each tribe took a path. When Pharaoh came and saw the paths in the sea and the water standing, he led them to imagine that the sea had done that out of awe of him; so he and his companions entered, and the sea closed over them.

nahhas-irab:80-80.t:
i.e. We commanded Mūsā ﷺ to command you to go out with him, so that He would speak to him in your presence and you would hear the speech.
وَنَزَّلْنا عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوى i.e. in the wilderness.

nahhas-irab:81-81.t:
i.e. let not abundance and well-being lead you to disobey, because «الطغيان» (transgression) is going beyond into what is not due.
فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِي وَمَنْ يَحْلِلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِي فَقَدْ هَوى Most of the Kufans read «يحلُل» (with ḍamma). Abū ʿUbayd and others reported that one says «حلّ يحِلّ» when something becomes due, and «حلّ يحُلّ» when it descends. The two meanings are close, except that the kasra is preferable because they agree on His saying: وَيَحِلُّ عَلَيْهِ عَذابٌ مُقِيمٌ [al-Zumar: 40]. Abū Isḥāq said: فَقَدْ هَوى means "he has perished; he has gone to al-Hāwiya," which is the bottom of the Fire.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: Wakīʿ said, from Sufyān: We used to hear concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic: وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ لِمَنْ تابَ i.e. from polytheism, وَآمَنَ i.e. after polytheism, وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً he prayed and fasted, ثُمَّ اهْتَدى he died in that state. This is the best that has been said on the verse. Al-Farrāʾ said: ثُمَّ اهْتَدى means he knew that there is reward for that and punishment for [failing in] it.

nahhas-irab:83-83.t: — the verse — He was commanded to command his people to go out with him so that they might hear the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:84-84.t: قالَ هُمْ أُولاءِ عَلى أَثَرِي i.e. they are close to me. Abū Ḥātim said: ʿĪsā said: Banū Tamīm say «هم أولى», unrestricted (mursala) and shortened, and the people of the Ḥijāz say أُولاءِ, lengthened. Al-Farrāʾ reported «هم أولاي على أثري» [Translator's note: the source writes «هم أولاء»; the following discussion, comparing it to «هداي» and speaking of annexation, shows the form «أولاي» is meant]. Abū Isḥāq claimed that this has no justification, and it is as he said, because this is not something that is annexed so as to be like «هداي». It cannot escape one of two possibilities: either it is a vague noun (demonstrative), and annexing it is impossible; or it is in the sense of «الذي», and then it is not annexed either, because what follows it is part of its completion and it is definite. ʿĪsā read هُمْ أُولاءِ عَلى أَثَرِي [Translator's note: i.e. «إِثْرِي», as the gloss shows], which means the same as «أثر». وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضى i.e. I hastened to go to the place to which You commanded me to go, so that You would be pleased with me.

nahhas-irab:85-85.t: قالَ فَإِنَّا قَدْ فَتَنَّا قَوْمَكَ مِنْ بَعْدِكَ i.e. We tested them and tried them as to whether they would find their way to Allah. وَأَضَلَّهُمُ السَّامِرِيُّ i.e. he called them to error and they followed him.

nahhas-irab:86-86.t:
فَرَجَعَ مُوسى إِلى قَوْمِهِ غَضْبانَ أَسِفاً As a ḥāl (circumstantial). قالَ يا قَوْمِ أَلَمْ يَعِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ وَعْداً حَسَناً He, Mighty and Majestic, promised them Paradise if they remained in His obedience, and promised them that He would let them hear His speech.
أَفَطالَ عَلَيْكُمُ i.e. did the time in which He would fulfil His promise to you seem long to you, so that you imagined He would not fulfil it? Its reality in grammar is: "Did the fulfilment of the covenant seem long to you?" فَأَخْلَفْتُمْ مَوْعِدِي because they had promised him that they would remain in obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:87-87.t:
قالُوا ما أَخْلَفْنا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنا i.e. it was said: this is general, with the particular intended; i.e. those who remained firm in obedience to Allah said: "We did not break our promise to you by our own power," i.e. we did not have the power to turn them back from worshipping the calf.
وَلكِنَّا حُمِّلْنا أَوْزاراً مِنْ زِينَةِ الْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْناها i.e. carrying the jewellery we had with us became burdensome to us, so we threw it into the fire to melt. فَكَذلِكَ أَلْقَى السَّامِرِيُّ The kāf is in the position of an accusative, i.e. "and al-Sāmirī threw a throwing like that."

nahhas-irab:88-88.t: فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا جَسَداً It was said: its meaning is "embodied and huge"; and it was said: its meaning is "a body with no spirit in it." لَهُ خُوارٌ because he pierced and perforated it, contriving to make sound come out of it.

nahhas-irab:89-89.t: أَفَلا يَرَوْنَ أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا in the sense of "that it does not return to them." Abū Isḥāq said: أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا in the accusative [«يرجعَ»] is also permissible, making it accusative through «أن». The nominative is preferable, and we have mentioned it.

nahhas-irab:90-90.t: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ الرَّحْمنُ The noun (ism) of «إنّ» and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:91-91.t: لَنْ نَبْرَحَ عَلَيْهِ عاكِفِينَ The khabar (predicate) of «نبرح», and [it is also said to be] a ḥāl (circumstantial). حَتَّى يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْنا مُوسى Accusative through «حتى»; the nominative is not permissible because it is future and nothing else.

nahhas-irab:92-93.t: أَلَّا تَتَّبِعَنِ i.e. that you did not join me. أَفَعَصَيْتَ أَمْرِي because he had commanded him to join him with them.

nahhas-irab:94-94.t:
لَ يَا بْنَ أُمَ
With fatḥa, it makes the two nouns a single noun; and with the genitive, by annexation. Abū Isḥāq said: Outside the Qurʾān «يا ابن أمّي» with yāʾ is permissible. تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِي وَلا بِرَأْسِي
i.e. do not do this, lest they imagine that it is contempt and punishment from you. It has also been said that Mūsā, peace be upon him, did this without contempt or punishment, just as a person takes hold of his own beard; and Allah knows best what He meant regarding His Prophet ﷺ. نِّي خَشِيتُ أَنْ تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ
i.e. I feared that if I went out and left them — when you had commanded me to go out with them — you would say: "You caused division among them and did not observe my word," because you had commanded me to be with them. [Translator's note: the Quranic fragments are cut as in the source («لَ يَا بْنَ أُمَ», «تَأْخُذْ», «نِّي»).]

nahhas-irab:95-95.t: Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. what is your affair, about which you are being addressed?

nahhas-irab:96-96.t:
قالَ بَصُرْتُ بِما لَمْ يَبْصُرُوا بِهِ He had seen Jibrāʾīl ﷺ when he descended to Mūsā ﷺ, and he thought that he thereby had a merit over them. So he took a handful from the track of Jibrāʾīl's mount, peace be upon him, and threw it into the calf. He did this only to make them imagine that the calf must be venerated for this reason. Abū Isḥāq said:
«قُبضة» is also permissible, like «غُرفة». «القُبضة» is the measure of what fills the palm, and «القَبضة» with fatḥa is the full of the whole palm.
Al-Ḥasan read «فَقَبَصْتُ قَبْصَةً» [Translator's note: the source shows «فَقَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةً» with ḍād; the gloss "with the fingertips" indicates the ṣād reading «قبصة»] and explained it as with the fingertips.

nahhas-irab:97-97.t:
[«لا مِساس»] is on the basis of generic negation (al-tabriya). Hārūn said: The dialect of the Arabs is «لا مَساسِ», with kasra on the sīn and fatḥa on the mīm. The grammarians have discussed this. Sībawayh holds that it is indeclinable (mabnī) on kasra, just as one says «اضربِ الرّجل». Abū Isḥāq explained this, saying: «لا مساس» is a negation, and the sīn was given kasra because kasra is a sign of the feminine — you say «فعلتِ يا امرأة». I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: When a word is defective in three respects it must be made indeclinable, and when it is defective in two respects it must be a diptote, because after diptote status there is nothing but indeclinability. «مساس» and «دراك» are defective in three respects: they are shifted from their pattern (maʿdūl), they are feminine, and they are definite. Since indeclinability was required in them, and the alif before the sīn is vowelless, the sīn was given kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, just as one says «اضربِ الرجل». Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw Abū Isḥāq holding that this view is mistaken, and he bound Abū al-ʿAbbās, if he named a woman «فرعون», to make it indeclinable — and no one says that. The Basrans read وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِداً لَنْ تُخْلَفَهُ with kasra on the lām [i.e. «تُخْلِفَهُ»]. It allows two meanings. One: "you will not find it broken," as one says «أحمدته», i.e. I found him praiseworthy. The other meaning is by way of threat, i.e. you must inevitably come to it. In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd, Allah's mercy be upon him: الَّذِي ظَلْتَ with kasra on the ẓāʾ. One says:
«ظللت أفعل ذاك» when you did it during the day, and «ظَلت» and «ظِلت»: one who says «ظَلت» dropped the lām for lightness, and one who says «ظِلت» cast the vowel of the lām onto the ẓāʾ. عاكِفاً The khabar (predicate). It is transmitted from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him: «لَنَحْرُقَنَّه», and likewise it is transmitted from Abū Jaʿfar; al-Ḥasan read «لنحرقنّه» ] [Translator's note: the source does not vowel these variants, and the bracket is as in the source]; and from the rest of the people: لَنُحَرِّقَنَّهُ. One says «حرَقه يحرُقه» and «يحرِقه» when one files it with a file or the like; «أحرقه يحرقه» with fire; and «حرّقه يحرّقه» may come from both of them, by way of intensification.

nahhas-irab:98-98.t: It is transmitted from Qatāda that he read وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْماً [Translator's note: i.e. «وَسَّعَ», with a doubled sīn, as the gloss shows], i.e. He filled it.

nahhas-irab:99-99.t: كَذلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْباءِ ما قَدْ سَبَقَ The kāf is in the position of an accusative, and the meaning is: "We relate to you just as We related to you the story of Mūsā, peace be upon him, and Pharaoh and al-Sāmirī." آتَيْناكَ مِنْ لَدُنَّا ذِكْراً كَذلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْباءِ ما قَدْ سَبَقَ The kāf is in the position of an accusative, and the meaning is: "We relate to you just as We related to you the story of Mūsā, peace be upon him, and Pharaoh and al-Sāmirī." آتَيْناكَ مِنْ لَدُنَّا ذِكْراً And it is the Qurʾān. [Translator's note: the passage is repeated in the source.]

nahhas-irab:100-100.t: مَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ i.e. and did not reflect on it and did not believe in it.

nahhas-irab:101-103.t: حِمْلًا as a specification (bayān), and زُرْقاً as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise قاعاً صَفْصَفاً. عَشْراً is accusative through «لبثتم»; the Kufans say regarding the meaning: "you remained only ten."

nahhas-irab:109-109.t: إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمنُ «من» is in the position of an accusative as an exception in which the excepted is outside the kind of the first.

nahhas-irab:110-110.t: Abū Isḥāq said: يَعْلَمُ ما بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ of the affair of the Hereafter and all that will be, وَما خَلْفَهُمْ what has already occurred of their deeds. Others said: the meaning of وَلا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِ عِلْماً is "and they do not encompass what we have mentioned"; and Allah knows best.

nahhas-irab:111-111.t: وَعَنَتِ الْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَيِّ الْقَيُّومِ There are two views on its meaning. One is that this is in the Hereafter. ʿIkrima transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās: وَعَنَتِ الْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَيِّ الْقَيُّومِ — he said: bowing and prostration. The meaning of «عنت» in the language is "submitted and obeyed"; from it comes «فتحت البلاد عنوة», i.e. by force. [Translator's note: only one of the two announced views is given in the source.]

nahhas-irab:117-117.t:
فَلا يُخْرِجَنَّكُما Figurative, i.e. do not accept from him, so that it becomes the cause of your expulsion. فَتَشْقى He did not say «فتشقيا» (dual), because the meaning is known, and Ādam ﷺ is the one addressed and intended. Al-Ḥasan said concerning His saying فَلا يُخْرِجَنَّكُما مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقى: he means the toil of this world; you see the son of Ādam only labouring.
Al-Farrāʾ said: It is that he eats from the toil of his own hands.

nahhas-irab:118-119.t: [«وأنّك لا تظمأ»] is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, Abū Jaʿfar, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī; ʿĀṣim and Nāfiʿ read «وإنك» with kasra on the hamza. The fatḥa is on the basis that «أنّ» forms a noun in the position of an accusative, conjoined to «أن» [in «إنّ لك ألّا تجوع»], the meaning being: "and you have [the promise] that you will not thirst in it." It may also be in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the position, the meaning being: "that is, that you will not thirst in it." The kasra is as a resumptive (istiʾnāf), or by conjunction to «إن لك».

nahhas-irab:121-121.t:
Al-Farrāʾ said: وَطَفِقا
in Arabic means "they set about." It was also said: they began to stick leaves upon themselves — fig leaves.
وَعَصى آدَمُ رَبَّهُ فَغَوى The yāʾ was changed to alif because it is voweled and what precedes it is voweled; for this reason the Kufans wrote it with yāʾ, to indicate its origin.

nahhas-irab:122-122.t: ثُمَّ اجْتَباهُ رَبُّهُ i.e. He chose him. فَتابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدى i.e. and guided him to repentance. Ḥammād ibn Salama transmitted from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr, from Abū Salama, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, فَإِنَّ لَهُ مَعِيشَةً ضَنْكاً [verse 124]: he said: the punishment of the grave.

nahhas-irab:128-128.t: أَفَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ i.e. does it not make clear to them? This is the reading of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Qatāda with yāʾ. [Translator's note: the source gives the standard text with yāʾ; the variant of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Qatāda is presumably «نهد» with nūn.] The grammarians have discussed it because it is difficult on account of the fāʿil (agent) of «يهد». Some of them said: «كم» is the agent; this is a mistake, because «كم» is interrogative, so what precedes it cannot act on it. Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is: "Has the matter not been made clear to them by Our destroying those We destroyed?" He said: The reality of «أفلم يهد لهم» is: "has it not been made clear to them with a clarity by which they are guided?" because they used to pass by the dwellings of ʿĀd and Thamūd; for that reason He, Mighty and Majestic, said: يَمْشُونَ فِي مَساكِنِهِمْ — and «في مسكنهم», as a maṣdar (verbal noun). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said, in what ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān related to us from him — and this is the sense of his words: he said: «يهدي» indicates guidance (al-hudā), so the agent is the guidance. Abū Isḥāq said: «كم» is in the position of an accusative through «أهلكنا». ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās: إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِأُولِي النُّهى — he said: for those of piety.

nahhas-irab:129-130.t: He said: لَكانَ لِزاماً i.e. death. وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «كلمة». The singular of «الآناء» is «إني»; the Basrans know no other. Al-Farrāʾ reported for the singular of «الآناء» «إنًى», shortened; [and] the singular of «الآنية» is «إناء», lengthened. Al-Farrāʾ, in this chapter of his book «المقصور والممدود» (The Shortened and the Lengthened), has things — which he presented as having both shortened and lengthened forms, such as «الإناء» and «الإنى», «الوراء» and «الورى» — that were objected to against him; al-Aṣmaʿī, Ibn al-Sikkīt and the precise lexicographers transmitted them differently from what he transmitted. What is said about this is that he is trustworthy in what he transmits, except that most of what the Kufans heard was from people who were not eloquent.

nahhas-irab:131-131.t: وَلا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلى ما مَتَّعْنا بِهِ أَزْواجاً مِنْهُمْ They are the rich, i.e. do not look at what the disbelievers have been given in this world. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read زَهْرَةَ with fatḥa on the hāʾ [i.e. «زَهَرَة»]. Abū Isḥāq said: «زهرة» is accusative through the sense of «متّعنا», because its meaning is "We made the life of this world an adornment for them." لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ i.e. that We may test them and make worship harder for them, because humility is hard for the rich and the trial upon them is harder. وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقى Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. the reward of your Lord. Al-Kisāʾī reported أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِمْ بَيِّنَةُ ما فِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولى [verse 133], and he said: on this basis بَيِّنَةُ ما فِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولى is also permissible [Translator's note: the source does not show the vowelling of the variants; the following explanation refers to «بيّنةٌ» with tanwīn and «بيّنةً» in the accusative]. Abū Jaʿfar said: If you give «بيّنة» tanwīn and the nominative, you make «ما» a badal (substitute) from it; and if you make it accusative, it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The meaning is: "Has not what is in the former scriptures come to them as a clear proof?"

nahhas-irab:134-134.t: وَلَوْ أَنَّا أَهْلَكْناهُمْ بِعَذابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ It was said: before the revelation. Al-Farrāʾ said: before the Messenger. فَنَتَّبِعَ آياتِكَ The answer of «لولا».

nahhas-irab:135-135.t:
Abū Isḥāq said: فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَصْحابُ — «من» is in the position of a nominative. Al-Farrāʾ said:
It may be in the position of an accusative, like وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْمُفْسِدَ مِنَ الْمُصْلِحِ [al-Baqara: 220]. Abū Isḥāq said: This is a mistake, because what precedes an interrogative cannot act on it, and «من» here is interrogative, since the meaning is: "You will know whether the people of the path are we or you." Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَصْحابُ الصِّراطِ السَّوِيِّ on the pattern fuʿlā without hamza [Translator's note: i.e. «السُّوى»; the source shows the standard vowelling]; making «الصراط» feminine is anomalous and rare. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: اهْدِنَا الصِّراطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ [al-Fātiḥa: 6], so it came masculine in this and elsewhere. Abū Ḥātim rejected this, saying: If it is from «السوء» (evil), it must be «السوءى»; and if it is from «السواء» (evenness), he must say «السِّيّى» with kasra on the sīn, the original being «السويا». Abū Jaʿfar said: The justification of the reading of Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and al-Jaḥdarī is that the original is «السوءى»; the vowelless letter is not a firm barrier, so it is as if he changed the hamza [to match] the ḍamma and replaced it — the vowelless letter not being a barrier — with an alif when what precedes it has fatḥa [Translator's note: the passage is compressed and somewhat unclear in the source]. وَمَنِ اهْتَدى is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first «من».
Al-Farrāʾ holds that the meaning of «من أصحاب الصراط السّويّ» is "whoever did not go astray," and that the meaning of «ومن اهتدى» is "whoever went astray and then was guided."
